title: Quentin and the Crown
premise: Mara Pemberton fled her hedge-witch master with nothing but a talent for numbers, and now keeps the ledgers of the Gildenholt, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names sold back to their owners. When a dying courier named Quentin staggers into the counting-house clutching a map of the Sundered Marches, Mara discovers the guild's oldest contract: a covenant between the human realm and the hidden folk, broken a century ago and bleeding both worlds dry. The map marks where the covenant can be reforged, but only by two hands—one mortal-born, one bound to the other side—and Quentin, half-fae and hunted by those who broke the pact, cannot finish it alone. As guild masters, fae creditors, and Mara's vengeful old master converge on the Marches, the two must decide what each will surrender: Quentin his claim to a true name and home, Mara the safety of being no one at all. In the end they reforge the covenant not with blood or gold but with mutual debt freely carried, and Mara chooses belonging over anonymity while Quentin, nameless but chosen, becomes the bridge between realms.
about_author: Ada Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ledgers from the 1700s before turning to fantasy. She writes stories about people who count things—coins, debts, days—and what happens when the numbers stop adding up.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the Gildenholt's counting-house, Mara balances entries for bottled thunder and pawned shadows, revealing her gift for seeing the true price of everything—including her own flight from her master Aldous Crane. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she trusts numbers because people have always priced her cheaply.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Weighing Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A bleeding man collapses against the guild's threshold at closing bell, pressing a wax-sealed map into Mara's hands and gasping that 'the debt comes due at solstice.' Guild enforcers close in; she hides him among the vaults. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance—the first thing she has ever stolen.

chapters.title: Quentin
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Waking in the vault, he gives his name reluctantly: courier for the Seelie remnant, bearer of the Covenant Map, hunted since his masters were slaughtered. He recognizes Mara's hedge-witch training as the second hand the reforging requires. Beat: wary gratitude curdling into guilt—he has made her a target.

chapters.title: What the Guild Knows
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The guild mistress Veyra reveals the Gildenholt was founded to service the old covenant and has profited from its ruin; she offers protection in exchange for the map. Mara reads the fine print and finds an ownership clause. Beat: disillusionment—every sanctuary has a price tag.

chapters.title: Crane's Summons
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her old master Aldous Crane arrives under guild escort, claiming Quentin as his property per an ancient indenture. Mara watches the man who once owned her bargain over another soul. Beat: old terror resurfacing, and the cold clarity of recognizing her abuser's arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Map That Bleeds
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The map responds to fae blood, redrawing itself toward the Sundered Marches; Quentin confesses he is half-fae, unclaimed by either world, his name held in trust by the dead. Beat: raw vulnerability—identity as something he has never owned.

chapters.title: Terms of Escape
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara forges ledger entries to spirit Quentin out during the tithe auction, trading her savings and her clean record. Veyra lets them go—too easily. Beat: exhilaration of agency shadowed by the certainty of a trap.

chapters.title: Road Through Ashfall
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the road north, the pair barter passage with a caravan of the displaced, learning how the broken covenant starves border villages of luck, rain, and memory. Beat: growing partnership; Mara teaches Quentin double-entry bookkeeping of favors owed.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At a river crossing, a fae toll-keeper demands a name as payment. Quentin offers fragments of himself; Mara instead negotiates a promissory note sealed in witch-oath. Beat: Mara sees Quentin's self-erasure clearly and refuses to let him pay it.

chapters.title: Crane's Hounds
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Crane's bound hounds ambush them; Mara uses hedge-craft her master taught her—turning his own lessons against his servants—for the first time. Beat: fury transmuted into power; the past becomes a weapon rather than a wound.

chapters.title: The Unmappable Mile
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They reach territory the map cannot render, where the Sundered Marches bleed through. Quentin experiences the pull of the fae side he inherited and nearly loses himself; Mara anchors him by reciting their shared ledger of debts. Beat: intimacy forged in near-loss.

chapters.title: Court of Outstanding Balances
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a twilight market of the hidden folk, they seek the covenant's terms and learn the reforging requires 'a debt freely carried by both hands'—and that Veyra has already filed a claim on the outcome. Beat: dread; every ally is also a creditor.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cornered by Crane, Mara bargains: her apprenticeship-debt, still legally binding, in exchange for Quentin's freedom. She signs herself back into bondage to buy his passage. Beat: sacrifice as choice, reclaiming the contract that once caged her.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Alone at the covenant-stone, Quentin confronts the ghost of his fae mother, who offers him a true name and a place—if he abandons the reforging and lets the human side stay severed. Beat: temptation of belonging without cost.

chapters.title: Veyra's Claim
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Escaping Crane with unexpected help from a repentant enforcer, Mara learns Veyra intends to reforge the covenant with the guild as sole intermediary—monetizing both worlds forever. Beat: righteous anger; the scale of what they're really fighting.

chapters.title: Two Hands
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara arrives at the stone as the solstice gate opens; Quentin must choose between the offered name and the half-mortal standing in the snow. He refuses the name. Beat: the emotional climax of identity—choosing made-over-bought belonging.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The ritual demands a debt freely carried by both hands: Mara's signed bond to Crane and Quentin's nameless trust in her, spoken aloud and exchanged. The covenant seals through them—but Crane arrives to enforce his claim mid-rite. Beat: terror and transcendence entwined.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With the covenant renewed, its law supersedes all lesser contracts: Crane's indenture dissolves, and the covenant itself judges his centuries of extracted debts. Beat: catharsis—not vengeance, but accounting; every entry balanced.

chapters.title: What Veyra Owes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Back at the Gildenholt, Veyra's monopoly scheme collapses under the new covenant's open-ledger clause. She concedes with poisoned grace, and the guild's impossible inventory is opened to the border villages. Beat: quiet triumph; systems can be rewritten.

chapters.title: A Name, Freely Given
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the counting-house, Mara enters a final line: Quentin, given a new name of her coining, entered as partner rather than asset. He accepts it as the first name anyone has handed him without a price. Beat: tenderness; identity as a gift between equals.

chapters.title: The Open Ledger
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Spring returns to the Marches; rain falls where luck had dried up. Mara and Quentin walk the border villages auditing the covenant's first honest season, welcomed at firesides. Beat: belonging earned and shared; the world mending at its seams.

chapters.title: Balance Carried Forward
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. In the counting-house at dusk, Mara opens a fresh ledger whose first page holds two names and no debts between them—only a single shared entry marked 'carried forward.' Somewhere beyond the door, the hidden folk knock politely. Beat: peace with the door left open; survival was the beginning, not the price.
